back: A change in direction when a wave enters a new medium at an angle, caused by a change in speed.
The spreading out of waves as they pass through a gap or around an edge.

front: Water waves going from deep to shallow water?
back: Speed and wavelength decrease; frequency unchanged; they bend towards the normal.

front: Which wave quantity never changes when a wave enters a new medium?
When is diffraction through a gap greatest?
back: When the gap is about the same size as the wavelength.

front: How does wavelength affect diffraction at an edge?
back: Longer wavelengths diffract (bend round the edge) more.

front: What does reflection change about a wave?
back: Only its direction: angle of incidence = angle of reflection; wavelength, frequency and speed are unchanged.
